Select features by size

selectSize.Rd

Select the largest or smallest polygons or lines in a SpatVector, optionally providing a maximum number of selected features, filtering by a size threshold, dissolving adjacent features, and/or splitting multipart features into single parts.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'SpatVector'
selectSize(x, n=Inf, largest=TRUE, threshold=NULL,
           dissolve=FALSE, singleparts=TRUE)

Arguments

x

SpatVector of polygons or lines

n

optional integer value (default Inf) indicating the maximum number of largest or smallest features to select (if they pass the optional threshold)

largest

if TRUE (default) select the largest feature(s), otherwise the smallest

threshold

optional size threshold (area in square meters for polygons, length in meters for lines) above which (if largest=TRUE or below which (if largest=FALSE features should be selected

dissolve

if TRUE, aggregate features before selection. Default FALSE

singleparts

if TRUE (default), split multipart features into individual parts before selection

Details

Polygon size is calculated using expanse; line size is calculated using perim. The threshold is applied before selecting the requested number of features. If fewer than n features satisfy the threshold, only qualifying features are returned.

If dissolve=TRUE, features are aggregated before size calculation. If singleparts=TRUE, multipart features are disaggregated before size calculation.

Value

SpatVector containing the selected features.

Author

A. Márcia Barbosa

See also

expanse, perim, selectHighest

Examples

f <- system.file("ex/lux.shp", package="terra")
v <- vect(f)

# Select the five largest polygons
large5 <- selectSize(v, n=5)

# Select the three smallest polygons
small3 <- selectSize(v, n=3, largest=FALSE)

# Select up to 4 largest polygons satisfying a given minimum area
large <- selectSize(v, n=4, threshold=260e+6)

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
plot(v)
polys(large5, col="red")
polys(small3, col="blue")
polys(large, col="gold", density=50)
} # }
